name: @wippy-session/wippy-form-answers
title: Session Form Answers
description: Invisible carrier element the Session server writes into a user's chat message after they answer a form, so the raw JSON answer record stays readable to the agent without ever being shown to the user.

wippy.description: Invisible carrier element. The Session server writes this tag into a user's chat message immediately after they answer a form, carrying the raw JSON answer record (form_id, form_version, title, late, answers) in its `record` attribute — e.g. `Answered questions about the delivery of your order.` followed by `<wippy-form-answers record='{...}'></wippy-form-answers>` (a single-line JSON string; the server escapes `'`, `<`, `>`, and `&` inside it so it round-trips through HTML attribute parsing intact). The record lives in the attribute, never in text content or children: an element that the chat sanitizer strips (e.g. because the Host's components list hasn't picked up this tag yet) or that hasn't finished loading its script (still an unrecognized element) both render nothing when they have no children — but would leak the raw JSON straight to the user if it were text content instead. `record` is declared as a prop specifically so the Host adds it to the sanitizer's allowed attribute list; without that, the attribute would still get stripped even once the tag itself is allowed through. The message is rendered as Markdown then sanitized; the answered-form card already shown above the message is the human-readable summary, so this element's entire purpose is to keep the JSON reachable in the raw message text for the agent to read back on a later turn, while staying invisible to the user under every failure mode. It renders nothing: no `<slot>` is ever created (so even stray light-DOM content would never project into the shadow root) and `:host { display: none; }` hides the element outright as defense in depth for the case where it does mount normally. Its only prop is `record` (string), it dispatches no events and opens no network requests, makes no host API calls of its own (its WippyElement base class does subscribe to the Host's @theme broadcast, invisibly, for consistent light/dark handling — that has no visible effect here since the element renders nothing), and exposes no parts, tokens, or classes to restyle — there is nothing to style. Its only public surface is a read-only `answerRecord` getter that parses that attribute and returns the parsed object, or `null` on empty or invalid JSON; it never throws. The element deliberately owns no `record` property: the Host's chat compiles message HTML as a Vue template, and Vue writes a custom element's prop as a DOM property when one of that name exists, which would swallow the value instead of setting the attribute. Agents must never emit this tag themselves — it is written exclusively by the Session server's message-composition code, never by agent-generated content.

record.description: The self-contained JSON answer record (form_id, form_version, title, late, answers) as a single-line string, written into this attribute by the Session server immediately after a form is answered. The server escapes `'`, `<`, `>`, and `&` inside the JSON so the attribute value round-trips through HTML parsing intact; getAttribute('record') returns it already unescaped. Agents never write this attribute themselves.
